memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""But on that day I will deal differently with the land of Goshen, where my people live; no swarms of flies will be there, so that you will know that I, the Lord, am in this land. I will make a distinction between my people and your people. This sign will occur tomorrow.'"" - Exodus 8:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the first time, God draws a clear line. Goshen, where Israel lives, will be untouched.

This is not because Israel deserved it. The following chapters show a people who grumble constantly. The distinction is entirely God's doing and rests on His covenant, not their merit.

We should be careful how we apply this. It is not a promise that believers will be exempt from every trouble. Christians get ill, lose jobs, and suffer in wars along with everyone else. Jesus said plainly that in this world we will have trouble (Jn 16:33), and He said the Father sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous alike.

But the deeper distinction is real and permanent. Those who belong to God are marked as His. Paul says God's solid foundation stands firm, sealed with this inscription: the Lord knows those who are His (2 Tim 2:19).

There is a day coming when the distinction will be complete. In the meantime, we live in a world of flies, marked by grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rest in belonging to God, or in being spared from difficulty?
2. What difference does it make to know that God knows those who are His?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I belong to You. Whatever falls on this world, keep me secure in Your hand. Amen.
